payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_follow_up.py::test_a_draft_declaring_depends_on_is_judged_minted_and_recorded_with_those_lines_cut stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/follow_up.py. The claim was "`follow_up.write_follow_ups` cuts the lines of each top-level `depends_on` and `consumes` key spelled bare at the start of its line from a parsed draft's frontmatter, before `_validate` reads it, when the draft declares a `depends_on` entry. Every other line stays as the writer sent it, the body and block scalars included. The cut holds only when the cut text parses to the draft's own spec with `depends_on` and `consumes` emptied. `_validate`, `cite`, `judge`, `send_back`'s quoted draft, the minted and the returned `Candidate`'s `spec` and `spec_sha`, and the recorded `follow_up` text all read the cut text. A cut that does not hold leaves the draft as the writer sent it, so `_validate` pools it with `declares a depends_on entry`. The witness drives seven groups. The first declares both keys in the flow form, and the second both in the indented block form. Both drafts of the third declare the indentless block form, and its first is judged red and sent back. The fourth also declares a budget above its origin's. The fifth reads its `depends_on` value again through a YAML alias, so its cut text does not parse. The sixth declares an empty list, which names no entry. The seventh puts a column-0 comment inside its `depends_on` list, so the cut would move its entry into `forbidden`.", and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
